Run seurat t-SNE

Source: R/scrna-clustering.R
RunSeuratTSNE.Rd

In addition to Seurat::RunTSNE(), we provide an additional argument to use markers as features for t-SNE, which makes the t-SNE more separated for different clusters.

Usage

RunSeuratTSNE(object, RunTSNEArgs = list(), cache = NULL, log = NULL)

Arguments

object

Seurat object

RunTSNEArgs

Arguments to pass to Seurat::RunTSNE(). RunTSNEArgs$features can be a character vector of features directly used for t-SNE, or a list with the following fields:

  • order: The order of the markers to use for t-SNE, e.g. "desc(abs(avg_log2FC))"

  • n: The number of total features to use for t-SNE, e.g. 30 If RunTSNEArgs$features is a list, it will run RunSeuratDEAnalysis() to get the markers for each group, and then select the top n/ngroups features for each group based on the order field. If RunTSNEArgs$features is a numeric value, it will be treated as the n field in the list above, with the default order being "desc(abs(avg_log2FC))".

cache

Directory to cache the all markers, which can be reused later if DE analysis is desired.

log

The logger to use. If NULL, a default logger will be used.

Value

The Seurat object with t-SNE results

Details

Scalar RunTSNEArgs$dims = N expands to 1:N. When both RunTSNEArgs$features and RunTSNEArgs$dims are provided, RunTSNEArgs$dims will be ignored and set to NULL. The features path always reads the default assay because Seurat::RunTSNE() has no assay argument. If neither RunTSNEArgs$features nor RunTSNEArgs$dims is provided, RunTSNEArgs$dims will be set to 1:min(30, ceiling(ncells/3), ncol(object@reductions[[reduction]])), where ncells is the number of cells in the object (or length(RunTSNEArgs$cells) when cells is set), and reduction is RunTSNEArgs$reduction (default: object@misc$integrated_new_reduction or "pca"). When RunTSNEArgs$perplexity is not provided, it defaults to max(1, min(30, floor((ncells - 1) / 3))) so small objects stay within Rtsne's perplexity bound.

On the dims path with tsne.method = "Rtsne", cells with identical coordinates in the selected embedding dimensions are deduplicated before the run: a warning reports how many cells are affected, t-SNE runs on the unique coordinates only, and each duplicate is then mapped onto its representative's coordinates, so the resulting reduction still covers every cell. RunTSNEArgs$cells (default: all cells) is narrowed to the representatives; the recorded command parameters then carry a dedup entry with the counts. If duplicate rows are only detected once Rtsne runs on the features path, its duplicate error is caught, a warning is emitted, and the run is retried once with check_duplicates = FALSE (duplicate cells may then overlap in the embedding). Duplicate cells never raise an error, even when RunTSNEArgs$check_duplicates = TRUE is supplied.

Examples

# \donttest{
obj <- RunSeuratTSNE(SeuratObject::pbmc_small, list(dims = 10))
#> WARN    [2026-11-24 23:53:45]   5 of 80 cells have identical coordinates in reduction 'pca' (dims 1:10); running t-SNE on the 75 unique cells and mapping each duplicate onto its representative's coordinates
#> INFO    [2026-11-24 23:53:45]   reduction=pca, dims=1:10, tsne.method=Rtsne, perplexity=24, reduction.name=tsne
#> Warning: Number of cells changing from 80 to 75
#> Warning: Number of cells changing from 75 to 80
# }
